statements.f1: The build farm coordinator runs on osk-farmctl-22; it hands out compile shards and holds the queue of pending build jobs.
statements.f2: We reprovisioned the coordinator onto faster local NVMe on 2026-04-08, so the build farm is now driven by osk-farmctl-07 and the old node went back into the worker pool.

topics.query: Which host runs the build farm coordinator now?

statements.f1: The patch CDN pulls from origin bucket osk-patchcdn-live2; edge nodes cache from there, and it holds every shipped build's delta files.
statements.f2: After the storage-account split on 2026-05-19, the patch CDN origin moved to osk-patches-prod-b to keep prod traffic off the staging uploads.

topics.query: What bucket is the patch CDN origin served from?

statements.f1: Ranked solo tickets enter matchmaking on osk.mm.rsolo.intake, which the solo matcher polls for eligible players.
statements.f2: The matchmaking rewrite on 2026-06-11 renamed the ranked solo intake to osk.mmq.solo-ranked, and producers were cut over in the same deploy.

topics.query: Which queue does ranked solo matchmaking use?

statements.f1: Dedicated-server game traffic uses UDP 31750-31820; the fleet firewall and the client both expect that range for gameplay packets.
statements.f2: To dodge a clash with a partner's relay, the game traffic port range moved to UDP 26900-26980 on 2026-07-14, with the firewall and the launcher updated together.

topics.query: What UDP port range does dedicated-server game traffic use?

statements.f1: Crash dumps are symbolicated against the symbol store bucket osk-symsrv-cold, where we keep PDBs for every public build.
statements.f2: Symbolication was slow pulling from cold storage, so on 2026-03-30 the symbol store was moved to osk-symstore-main on hot storage.

topics.query: Which bucket holds the symbols for crash dump symbolication?

statements.f1: The launcher fetches its runtime config from osk-lcfg-api1; that endpoint returns the feature flags and the current patch manifest URL.
statements.f2: The config service was moved behind the new core tier on 2026-08-05, so launchers now call osk-lcfg-core3 and the previous endpoint returns a redirect for one release.

topics.query: Which host serves the launcher configuration endpoint?

statements.f1: The nightly full build kicks off at 00:15 CET once the day's merges are frozen; it produces the clean baseline the depot upload runs against.
statements.f2: We shifted the nightly full build later, to 02:35 CET, on 2026-05-06 so it stops overlapping the EU backup window.

topics.query: What time does the nightly full build start?

statements.f1: Depot uploads go through osk-chunkpush, which chunks the build and pushes only the changed blocks to the depot.
statements.f2: The upload tooling was replaced on 2026-06-22; depot pushes now use osk-depotctl, which parallelises across depots and resumes cleanly after a drop.

topics.query: Which tool do we use to upload builds to the depot?

statements.f1: The EU dedicated-server fleet is primarily hosted in osk-eun-sto3, which carries most of the Nordic and northern-EU player load.
statements.f2: Latency to central Europe pushed us to move the EU fleet's primary region to osk-euw-fra2 on 2026-07-28, with the northern region kept as overflow.

topics.query: Where is the EU dedicated-server fleet primarily hosted?

statements.f1: Match replays are retained for 84 days, long enough for the ranked season review and most cheat reports.
statements.f2: Player demand for older replays pushed retention out to 364 days on 2026-04-25, with a move to cold storage after the first month.

topics.query: How long are match replays kept?

statements.f1: Casual matchmaking backfill allows a maximum MMR spread of 480 MMR when filling a dropped slot, trading match quality for a fast refill.
statements.d: Backfill only fires in the first two minutes of a casual match; after that the slot stays open and the game plays out short-handed.

topics.query: What's the maximum MMR spread allowed for casual matchmaking backfill?

statements.f1: Build farm pages go to osk-bf-pager; a red build or a stuck shard fans out there before it reaches the wider engineering channel.
statements.d: Build farm paging deduplicates repeat failures within a single run, so one flaky test can't storm the on-call.

topics.query: Which channel do build farm pages go to?

statements.f1: The primary on-call dashboard for live-ops monitoring is osk-ccu-geo, which maps concurrent players by region against fleet capacity.
statements.d: Live-ops monitoring builds its panels from the same metrics pipeline the analytics team uses, so a pipeline stall greys out both at once.

topics.query: What's the main on-call dashboard for live-ops monitoring?

statements.f1: Matchmaking is running ruleset mmcfg-r219, the revision that tightened role balance in ranked.
statements.f2: We rolled ruleset mmcfg-r236 to production on 2026-06-02 to trial wider party spreads.
statements.f3: Queue times regressed, so matchmaking was reverted to mmcfg-r219 on 2026-06-05.

topics.query: Which matchmaking ruleset revision is live?

statements.f1: Ban waves go out in the Fri 11:20 CET slot, timed so appeals land during the following support shift.
statements.f2: To catch weekend cheaters sooner, the ban wave was moved to Tue 15:30 CET on 2026-05-12.
statements.f3: Support coverage complained, so the ban wave went back to Fri 11:20 CET on 2026-05-26.

topics.query: When does the weekly anti-cheat ban wave run?

statements.f1: The launcher pins the anti-cheat client module at oskguard-3.9.4; clients that don't match are blocked from ranked.
statements.f2: We pinned oskguard-4.2.7 on 2026-07-09 to ship the new kernel-driver signature checks.
statements.f3: A compatibility break on older Windows builds forced a rollback to oskguard-3.9.4 on 2026-07-16.

topics.query: Which anti-cheat client version is currently pinned?

hard_negatives.text: The depot uploader's service token isn't in the repo; it lives in the secrets manager at secret/osk/depot/uploader and is injected as an env var by the CI runner.
The runbook screenshot shows the SMTP login masked as osk-mailer / ****, so substitute the real <password> from the vault before you test the alert path.
The reproducible build is pinned to commit 4904d4449e920a9a4be8d737edd828d150cd8cf5, a git commit sha rather than a secret; tag the release only once CI matches it.
Before promoting a patch to the live CDN, verify the manifest hash on two edge nodes, warm the cache in one region, and watch error rates for ten minutes before opening it wide.
Per OSK-REL-032 rev 4, every client build shipped to players must come from the build farm, never from a developer workstation.
Correction to yesterday's note: the login spike hit the account service, not the launcher config service; the launcher stayed healthy the whole window.
No one ships a depot build straight to the live branch without a canary; a bad patch there reaches every player at once and can't be cleanly rolled back mid-download.
A leaked upload token turned up in a public gist last month; we revoked it at once and rotated the depot credentials, and the ticket only ever quoted the osk_sec_**** prefix.
